AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the analgesic effect of a prilocaine + bupivacaine combination in patients undergoing periprostatic nerve block (PNB) by comparing its effects with those of prilocaine alone.

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: Single center, single-blind, prospective descriptive study.

AbstractText.Label: Subjects
AbstractText.content: Four hundred patients with transrectal prostate biopsy pain.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: The patients in this prospective, randomized controlled study were divided into two groups. The first group received prilocaine during PNB (Group 1), whereas the second received a prilocaine + bupivacaine combination (Group 2).

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: The mean visual analog scale (VAS) scores immediately after biopsy were 2.52 ± 0.7 and 2.53 ± 0.9, respectively (P = 0.35). VAS values were significantly lower in Group 2 at one and six hours following the procedure. The most painful part of the biopsy according to many patients was the probe insertion.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: The prilocaine + bupivacaine combination is an effective analgesic method during prostate biopsies and for one and six hours after prostate biopsy.

Article.ArticleTitle: A Comparison of Prilocaine vs Prilocaine + Bupivacaine in Periprostatic Block in Ambulatory Prostate Biopsies: A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Study.
